documents.title: Label-free multi-metric pipeline for reproducible clustering of single-cell RNA-seq cell types.
documents.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has transformed our ability to identify cell types and explore cellular diversity. However, determining whether apparent cell subtypes represent true biological populations or artifacts of data analysis remains a major challenge. To address this issue, we developed scClustBench, an open-source benchmarking framework that evaluates cluster quality, stability, and reproducibility across multiple analytical approaches. Rather than relying on a single clustering method, scClustBench tests whether proposed cell subtypes can be consistently recovered. We applied scClustBen

documents.title: Ultralow-volume shallow microwell-based collection and processing for scalable spatial proteome mapping of tissues.
documents.abstract: Multi-ome mapping technologies for precise comprehensive characterization of tissues at high spatial resolutions are crucial for providing insights into tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment within spatial context. However, proteome mapping technologies lag far behind other transcriptome (genome) mapping technologies. Here we report an Ultralow-volume, Shallow, Microwell plate-based voxel Collection and Processing coupled with mass spectrometry (MS) method, termed USMCP-MS, for robust scalable proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions. documents.title: Iterative Geometric Structure Guided Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Scheme for Bulk Tissue RNA-seq Data Deconvolution.
documents.abstract: Complete deconvolution is a class of unsupervised methods that aim to estimate both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles (GEPs) from bulk RNA-seq data, without requiring prior reference profiles. Hence, it enables broader applicability to tissues or species for which reference data are limited or unavailable. For many existing methods, nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) serves as the fundamental computational tool. documents.title: ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D Are associated with urea cycle activity and ammonia stress responses in prostate cancer.
documents.abstract: Prostate cancer (PRAD) progression is closely associated with metabolic reprogramming, but the role of nitrogen metabolism and ammonia-associated cell death remains unclear. This study investigates the clinical and functional significance of urea cycle activity in PRAD.

documents.title: A versatile set of computational tools for inference of genetic ancestry from human molecular data.
documents.abstract: Molecular properties of human diseases and conditions often exhibit dependence on the genetic ancestry of the donor. In order to make more human molecular data available for ancestry-informed research, we developed a set of software tools termed Robust Ancestry Inference using Data Synthesis (RAIDS) for inference of genetic ancestry from sequence data that pose challenges to genotyping. The data-synthesis procedure, underlying RAIDS, makes it a unique tool capable of assessing and optimizing the accuracy of inference for each individual molecular profile, with no resort to cohort data. documents.title: SigBridgeR: An R Toolkit for Standardized Identification and Benchmarking of Phenotype-Associated Cell Subpopulations in Single-Cell Transcriptomics.
documents.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has revolutionized our understanding of cellular heterogeneity, yet linking specific cell subpopulations to clinically relevant phenotypes remains a major challenge. Although multiple computational methods have been developed to integrate bulk transcriptomic and single-cell data for phenotype-associated cell identification, differences in algorithmic strategies, parameter configurations, software implementations, and output formats make it difficult to compare methods fairly, reproduce analyses, and determine which approach is most suitable for a given bi

documents.title: Inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell perturbation data by optimizing causal reach of latent mediator dynamics.
documents.abstract: Resolving the causal structure of gene regulatory networks is central to understanding cellular regulation. Pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell RNA readouts measure the transcriptional consequences of many interventions in parallel, providing a powerful resource for causal discovery. Combinatorial designs that perturb multiple regulators per cell increase throughput and can reveal responses that single-gene perturbations do not. documents.title: Mapping the regulatory wiring of endothelial cell differentiation reveals a critical role for Hippo mechanosignaling.
documents.abstract: At each step of development, stem cells encounter a branching decision to differentiate into one type of cell or another. This decision is executed through the action of competing gene programs that specify different cellular identities. Consequently, creating a comprehensive map of the gene programs that drive each branching step of human cell differentiation remains a long-sought goal of developmental and stem cell biology. documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq.
documents.abstract: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. documents.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
documents.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. documents.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d

documents.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
documents.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod

documents.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
documents.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.

documents.title: An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.
documents.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.

documents.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
documents.abstract: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. documents.title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.
documents.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data used in epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often overlook hierarchical relationships among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-type hierarchy, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
documents.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. documents.title: CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis.
documents.abstract: The updated CellMarker 3.0 resource (http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CellMarker) offers a comprehensive resource, integrating experimentally validated and robustly algorithm-predicted marker genes for diverse cell types across human and mouse tissues. In addition, web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data are described. CellMarker 3.0 was updated with more data and new features, including (i) appending 274 tissues, 1877 cell types, 64 040 markers, and 1 245 923 tissue-cell type-marker entries over the previous version. documents.title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
documents.abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. documents.title: Integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics via the Scissor algorithm reveals APOE-dependent cholesterol metabolic reprogramming in macrophages associated with osimertinib resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: The tumor microenvironment contributes to acquired resistance against osimertinib in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the key cell subpopulations and the underlying metabolic mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated.

documents.title: A ten-gene tyrosine-metabolism signature defines prognosis and reveals metabo-immune suppression in low-grade astrocytoma.
documents.abstract: Emerging evidence implicates dysregulated tyrosine metabolism in glioma malignancy; however, its cell-type specificity and clinical relevance in low-grade astrocytoma (LGA) remain undefined.
